# Adjudication Task — Chapter 310

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃310화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|스스스슥.
  6|
  7|천력부의 등 뒤로 모습을 드러낸 산적들의 숫자는 오백을 헤아렸다.
  8|
  9|그러나 주화란의 얼굴이 차갑게 굳은 것은, 그들의 수가 압도적이기 때문만은 아니었다.
 10|
 11|‘기세가 달라.’
 12|
 13|산을 넘으려는 자와 막는 자. 표국과 녹림은 떼 놓을 수 없는 관계다.
 14|
 15|매번 칼을 빼 들 수는 없는 노릇이라 표국 측에서는 일정 금액의 통행료를 지불하고, 녹림 또한 적당한 선에서 물러나 서로의 체면을 지키는 것이 오랜 관례였다.
 16|
 17|그러나 천력부와 그가 이끄는 흑석채의 산적들에게서는 물러서려는 기미가 보이지 않았다.
 18|
 19|“당신은…… 끝내 피를 볼 생각이군요.”
 20|
 21|주화란의 말에 천력부가 입꼬리를 말아 올렸다.
 22|
 23|“어린 년이 눈치가 제법이로구나. 맞다. 내 오늘 흑석산을 피로 물들일 생각이니라.”
 24|
 25|“어린 년?”
 26|
 27|“왜, 마음에 안 들면 늙은 년이라 불러 주랴?”
 28|
 29|“나는 용봉표국의 소국주. 내가 당신에게 하듯, 당신도 예의를 갖추세요.”
 30|
 31|붓으로 그린 듯한 주화란의 아름다운 눈썹이 위로 솟구쳤다.
 32|
 33|용봉표국의 무남독녀지만 금이야 옥이야 자란 것만은 아니다.
 34|
 35|어린 시절부터 손바닥에 굳은살이 배기도록 검을 휘둘렀고, 표사들과 함께 길에서 먹고 자며 보고 배웠다.
 36|
 37|사람들은 강북삼화라며 주화란을 떠받들지만, 그녀는 온실 속 화초가 아니었다.
 38|
 39|“맹랑한 년이로고. 싫다면 어찌하겠느냐?”
 40|
 41|“그렇다면…….”
 42|
 43|비수를 숨긴 꽃, 은비화(隱匕花) 주화란이 서늘한 표정으로 말을 이었다.
 44|
 45|“죽어야지, 어린 년한테.”
 46|
 47|“뭐라? 으허, 으하하하하!”
 48|
 49|천력부의 광소가 멎은 것은 잠시 후였다.
 50|
 51|“생각보다는 강단이 있군. 마음에 들었다.”
 52|
 53|“늙은 산적 놈 마음에 들어 봤자 기쁘지도 않아.”
 54|
 55|“혓바닥이 제법 맵구나. 뒷일이 걱정되지 않느냐?”
 56|
 57|“도대체 왜 이런 짓거리를 벌이는 거지?”
 58|
 59|“왜냐니. 산적이 죽이고 빼앗겠다는데 별다른 이유라도 필요한 것이냐?”
 60|
 61|천력부의 능청스러운 대답에 주화란은 입술을 질끈 깨물었다.
 62|
 63|“이 일이 알려지면 녹림맹의 입장도 곤란해질 텐데.”
 64|
 65|“곤란해져?”
 66|
 67|“우리 용봉표국 또한 정파의 일원. 정파 무림이 가만히 있지 않을 테니까.”
 68|
 69|“정파의 일원이라. 그럼 곤란하지.”
 70|
 71|천력부가 덥수룩한 턱수염을 쓰다듬으며 말을 이었다.
 72|
 73|“그래서 알려지지 않도록 애써 볼 생각이다. 모든 비밀은 새어 나가지 않으면 그만 아니겠느냐?”
 74|
 75|“……!”
 76|
 77|살인멸구(殺人滅口).
 78|
 79|천력부의 말이 뜻하는 바를 알아차린 주화란은 검파를 힘껏 움켜쥐었다. 그런 그녀를 대신해 총표두 허준이 앞으로 나서며 외쳤다.
 80|
 81|“백 냥! 길을 터 준다면 은자 백 냥을 주지. 오늘 일은 불문(不問)에 부칠 테니 이쯤에서 멈추게!”
 82|
 83|“허어. 백 냥이나? 그것도 은자로?”
 84|
 85|“물론. 내가 지금껏 허언을 한 적이 있던가?”
 86|
 87|“그건 아니지. 우리가 한두 번 본 사이도 아니고. 허 표두라면 충분히 믿을 만해.”
 88|
 89|총 표두 허준은 삼십 년에 가까운 세월을 용봉표국에 몸담았다.
 90|
 91|용봉표국은 섬서에 기반을 둔 대형 표국. 그곳에서 크고 작은 수백 회의 표행을 성공시킨 그는 흑석산을 자주 넘나들며 녹림의 채주들과 안면을 텄고, 오 년 전 새롭게 채주가 된 천력부와도 마찬가지였다.
 92|
 93|“평소 통행료의 다섯 배야. 짓궂은 장난은 그만하고 이만 길을 터 주게.”
 94|
 95|“짓궂은 장난이라. 그렇게 보였나?”
 96|
 97|너털웃음을 터트린 천력부의 얼굴에 돌연 한기가 서렸다.
 98|
 99|“사람을 병신으로 봐도 유분수지. 이봐, 허 표두. 값은 제대로 쳐야지.”
100|
101|“가, 값을 제대로 치다니?”
102|
103|“지금 운송 중인 표물에 천년설삼(千年雪蔘)이 있다는 건 우리 산채에서 기르는 개새끼도 알아. 당장 장물로 팔아 치워도 은자 수천 냥은 너끈히 받아 낼 물건이지. 안 그런가?”
104|
105|“……!”
106|
107|그 순간, 주화란과 허준을 포함한 몇몇의 눈꺼풀이 파르르 떨렸다.
108|
109|천년설삼은 완전히 소화한다면 능히 일 갑자의 공력을 얻을 수 있다는 영약.
110|
111|종남파에서 비밀리에 의뢰한 천년설삼의 존재는 용봉표국 내에서도 극소수만이 아는 특급 기밀 사항이다.
112|
113|그런데 어찌 천력부에 귀에 들어갔단 말인가.
114|
115|‘우연이 아니었어.’
116|
117|주화란의 뇌리에 지난 넉 달간의 표행이 스쳤다.
118|
119|철천지원수라도 만난 듯 덤벼들던 산적들과 이름 모를 낭인들.
120|
121|크고 작은 수십 회의 전투를 치르며 큰 희생을 감내해야 했던 이유는 바로 천년설삼에 대한 정보가 흘러 나갔기 때문이었다.
122|
123|‘도대체 누가?’
124|
125|설마 하는 생각은 했었다. 그러나 애써 의심을 억눌렀다.
126|
127|지난 이 년간 겹치고 겹친 악재에서 그녀를 견딜 수 있게 해 준 원동력은 바로 주위의 사람들이었으니까.
128|
129|할아버지가 아버지에게, 아버지가 자신에게 물려준 가장 큰 재산.
130|
131|용봉표국이 과거의 위상을 잃고 점점 기울어지는데도 그들은 떠나지 않았다. 계속해서 실패를 겪는 자신에게 아낌없는 신뢰와 지지를 보여 주었다.
132|
133|그래서 더더욱 그런 이들을 의심하고 싶지 않았다. 의심하기 싫었다.
134|
135|‘하지만 이제는…….’
136|
137|주화란은 공허한 눈빛으로 주위를 훑었다.
138|
139|그녀만큼이나 큰 배신감을 느낀 채 굳어 버린 총표두 허준. 그리고 천년설삼의 존재를 아는 세 사람이 눈에 들어왔다.
140|
141|용봉표국을 대표하는 뛰어난 세 명의 표두. 이른바 용봉삼표(龍鳳三鏢)라 불리는 이들이었다.
142|
143|‘석칠. 노필중.’
144|
145|마흔 줄에 접어든 두 명의 중년 표두를 스친 주화란의 시선이 마지막 한 사람을 향했다.
146|
147|‘송일섬.’
148|
149|송일섬은 용봉삼표의 다른 두 사람과는 달리 훤칠하고 잘생긴 외모의 소유자였다.
150|
151|이제 갓 이립을 넘긴 젊은 나이의 그는 십 년 전 용봉표국에 표사로 입문하여 승승장구했다.
152|
153|간혹 거친 성미를 드러내기도 했으나 뛰어난 무공으로 표행을 성공적으로 이끌었기에 젊은 나이임에도 용봉삼표로 불릴 수 있었다.
154|
155|그러나 그런 송일섬에게는 무성한 뒷말이 따라다녔다.
156|
157|
158|
159|‘낭인 출신이래. 그것도 해결사.’
160|
161|‘보수만 받으면 무슨 짓이든 마다하지 않았다더군.’
162|
163|‘그뿐인가? 아가씨를 깊이 연모하고 있다는 소문이 파다해. 지난번 시비인 미향이가 알려 줬는데, 틈만 나면 내원으로 들어와 정원을 서성거린다더라고.’
164|
165|‘표국에 들어온 이유도 아가씨 때문이라던데…… 다들 아는 사실이지만 국주님께서 표사 사윗감을 원하지 않았나.’
166|
167|
168|
169|주화란도 알고 있었다. 송일섬을 둘러싼 공공연한 소문을. 그리고 그들의 말이 대부분 사실임을.
170|
171|가끔 느껴지는 송일섬의 노골적인 시선에 마음이 불편했던 적도 있었다. 그런 이유로 이번 표행에 그를 기용할지 고민한 것도 사실이었다.
172|
173|‘하지만 설마 송 표두가…….’
174|
175|주화란의 시선이 송일섬의 얼굴에 머무른 바로 그 순간, 사나워 보이는 그의 굵은 눈썹이 위로 솟구쳤다.
176|
177|번쩍, 쐐애애애액!
178|
179|“화란아!”
180|
181|세 가지 일이 동시에 일어났다.
182|
183|송일섬의 소맷자락에서 한 자루의 비수가 튀어나온 것. 동시에 총 표두 허준이 다급하게 주화란의 앞을 가로막은 것.
184|
185|마지막으로…….
186|
187|푹!
188|
189|“커헉, 크르륵.”
190|
191|이십여 장 밖. 목에 비수가 꽂힌 흑석채의 산적 하나가 풀썩 고꾸라진 것.
192|
193|피거품을 토해 낸 산적은 부르르 몸을 떨더니 이내 숨을 거두었다.
194|
195|“……!”
196|
197|싸늘한 적막이 내려앉은 장내. 끝나지 않을 것 같던 침묵을 깨트린 것은 송일섬의 한 마디였다.
198|
199|“문답무용! 모두 죽을 각오로 싸워라!”
200|
201|사나운 외침이 밤바람을 타고 멀리 퍼져 나가자 주화란과 허준, 그리고 용봉표국의 모두는 깨달았다.
202|
203|이미 협상은 물 건너갔다는 것을. 뜻하지 않게 선공을 당한 수백의 적들과 목숨을 건 일전을 펼쳐야 한다는 것을.
204|
205|“송일섬! 이게 무슨 짓이냐!”
206|
207|총 표두 허준의 창노한 외침에 송일섬이 유엽도(柳葉刀)를 들어 어깨에 척 걸쳤다.
208|
209|“뭐 하는 짓이긴. 이제 와서 그걸 따지기에는 너무 늦었지 않소?”
210|
211|“네놈……!”
212|
213|“그의 말이 맞아요.”
214|
215|주화란은 덤덤한 목소리로 검파를 잡았다.
216|
217|애석하게도 송일섬의 말은 사실이었다.
218|
219|천력부가 무시무시한 기세를 흩뿌리며 그들을 향해 다가오고 있었으니까.
220|
221|손 쓸 새도 없이 수하 하나를 잃은 그의 부릅뜬 눈에서는 화염이 쏟아지고 있었다.
222|
223|“모조리 도륙을 내 주마.”
224|
225|츠츠츠츠!
226|
227|늘어트린 거대한 도끼에서 붉은 기가 넘실거렸다.
228|
229|무수히 많은 이들이 속해 있는 녹림맹. 그중에서도 서열 이십 위의 절정 고수가 바로 천력부였다.
230|
231|우두머리의 기세에 힘입은 오백 명의 녹림도 또한 산짐승처럼 으르렁거렸다.
232|
233|“전부 죽여!”
234|
235|“이 자리가 네놈들 무덤이다!”
236|
237|그 성난 외침을 들으며 주화란은 별이 총총히 박힌 밤하늘을 바라보았다.
238|
239|‘어쩌면…… 이곳이 마지막 표행이 될 수도 있겠구나.’
240|
241|남아 있는 칠십여 명의 인원 중 쟁자수를 제외한 표사의 숫자는 고작 사십여 명.
242|
243|모두가 오랜 표행으로 인해 지칠 대로 지쳐 있었다. 천력부와 오백의 녹림도를 감당하기에는 너무 가혹한 조건이다.
244|
245|‘내가 할 수 있을까?’
246|
247|두두두.
248|
249|수백의 발걸음에 땅이 진동한다. 피하고자 했으나 피할 수 없는 전투가 시작되려 하고 있었다.
250|
251|‘남은 건 마지막까지 싸우는 것뿐.’
252|
253|한 사람이라도 살려 보내야 한다.
254|
255|주화란이 고개를 바로 하려던 그때, 지금까지 보지 못했던 별 하나가 눈에 띄었다.
256|
257|캄캄한 밤하늘에 수놓아진 많은 별 중에서도 유독 밝게 빛나던 그것은, 아주 짧은 시간 광채를 뿌리더니 이내 사라졌다.
258|
259|그리고 다음 순간. 아무도 예상치 못했던 일이 벌어졌다.
260|
261|“모두 싸우지 마세요! 아무리 사이가 나빠도 싸우면 큰일 나요!”
262|
263|갑자기 들려온 누군가의 외침에 사람들의 신형이 우뚝 멈췄다. 이내 수백 명의 고개가 목소리가 들려온 방향을 향해 홱 돌아갔다.
264|
265|온통 어둠에 잠긴 세상.
266|
267|언덕 위에 우뚝 서 있는 네 사람의 신형이 희미한 달빛을 받아 빛나고 있었다.
268|
269|이내 두런두런 들려오는 목소리들.
270|
271|“쟤들 뭐야?”
272|
273|“산적 같은데요. 한쪽은 표국 사람들 같고.”

[P2]
*Rustle, rustle, rustle.*

[P3]
Five hundred bandits emerged behind Heavenly Axe.

[P4]
But their overwhelming numbers weren’t the only reason Ju Hwaran’s face hardened.

[P5]
*There’s something different about them.*

[P6]
Those who crossed the mountains and those who barred the way—Escort Bureaus and the Green Forest were inextricably linked.

[P7]
An Escort Bureau couldn’t draw its swords every time it encountered bandits, so it would pay a set toll. The Green Forest, in turn, would accept a reasonable sum and withdraw, allowing both sides to save face. That had long been the custom.

[P8]
But neither Heavenly Axe nor the bandits of Black Stone Stronghold showed any intention of backing down.

[P9]
“You mean to spill blood after all…”

[P10]
Heavenly Axe curled his lips at Ju Hwaran’s words.

[P11]
“You’re pretty sharp for a little bitch. That’s right. Today, I intend to stain Black Stone Mountain with blood.”

[P12]
“Little bitch?”

[P13]
“What? Don’t like it? Would you rather I called you an old bitch?”

[P14]
“I am the Young Bureau Head of the Yongbong Escort Bureau. Show me the same courtesy I’m showing you.”

[P15]
Ju Hwaran’s beautiful, brush-painted eyebrows shot upward.

[P16]
She was the bureau chief’s only child, but that didn’t mean she had been raised pampered and sheltered.

[P17]
She had swung a sword since childhood until calluses formed across her palms. She had eaten and slept on the road alongside the escorts, watching and learning.

[P18]
People fawned over Ju Hwaran as one of the Three Flowers of Jiangbei, but she was no hothouse flower.

[P19]
“What a brazen little bitch. And what will you do if I refuse?”

[P20]
“Then…”

[P21]
Ju Hwaran—the Dagger Hidden Flower—continued with a frosty expression.

[P22]
“You’ll have to die at the hands of this little bitch.”

[P23]
“What? Huh… Hahahahaha!”

[P24]
It took a while for Heavenly Axe’s wild laughter to subside.

[P25]
“You’ve got more backbone than I expected. I like you.”

[P26]
“Why would I care if some old bandit likes me?”

[P27]
“You’ve got quite the sharp tongue. Aren’t you worried about what comes next?”

[P28]
“Why are you doing this in the first place?”

[P29]
“Why? A bandit wants to kill and rob you. Does he need some special reason?”

[P30]
Ju Hwaran bit down hard on her lip at his brazen reply.

[P31]
“If word of this gets out, it will put the Green Forest Alliance in a difficult position.”

[P32]
“A difficult position?”

[P33]
“The Yongbong Escort Bureau is part of the orthodox faction. The orthodox Murim won’t stand idly by.”

[P34]
“Part of the orthodox faction, are you? Then I suppose that would be a problem.”

[P35]
Heavenly Axe stroked his shaggy beard.

[P36]
“So I’ll do my best to make sure word never gets out. A secret can’t hurt anyone if it never leaks, can it?”

[P37]
“…”

[P38]
*Silencing the Witnesses.*

[P39]
Realizing what Heavenly Axe meant, Ju Hwaran tightened her grip on her sword hilt. Chief Escort Heo Jun stepped forward in her place and shouted, “One hundred silver nyang! Clear the road, and I’ll give you one hundred silver nyang. We’ll consider today’s matter closed, so let this end here!”

[P40]
“Oh? A hundred nyang? In silver, no less?”

[P41]
“Of course. Have I ever made an empty promise?”

[P42]
“No, you haven’t. This is hardly our first meeting. Brother Heo’s word can be trusted.”

[P43]
Chief Escort Heo Jun had devoted nearly thirty years to the Yongbong Escort Bureau.

[P44]
The Yongbong Escort Bureau was a major Escort Bureau based in Shaanxi. Heo Jun had successfully completed hundreds of escort journeys, large and small, and crossed Black Stone Mountain so often that he had become acquainted with the Green Forest’s Stronghold Lords. That included Heavenly Axe, who had taken command of Black Stone Stronghold five years earlier.

[P45]
“That’s five times the usual toll. Enough of this nasty joke. Clear the road.”

[P46]
“A nasty joke? Is that what this looked like?”

[P47]
Heavenly Axe let out a hearty laugh. Then his face abruptly turned cold.

[P48]
“There’s a limit to how much of a fool you can take me for. Brother Heo, if you want to bargain, offer a fair price.”

[P49]
“A-A fair price?”

[P50]
“Even the dogs in my stronghold know that the goods you’re transporting include a Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng. We could sell it as stolen goods today and easily get several thousand silver nyang for it. Isn’t that right?”

[P51]
“…”

[P52]
Several people’s eyelids began to twitch, including Ju Hwaran’s and Heo Jun’s.

[P53]
The Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng was an elixir said to grant a full jiazi of internal energy if completely digested.

[P54]
Its transport had been secretly commissioned by the Zhongnan Sect, and its existence was a top-level secret known to only a handful of people within the Yongbong Escort Bureau.

[P55]
How had word reached Heavenly Axe?

[P56]
*None of it was a coincidence.*

[P57]
The past four months of the escort journey flashed through Ju Hwaran’s mind.

[P58]
The bandits and nameless wandering martial artists who had attacked them as if they were mortal enemies.

[P59]
They had fought dozens of battles, large and small, and suffered terrible losses—all because information about the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng had leaked.

[P60]
*Who was it?*

[P61]
The thought had occurred to her before, but she had forced her suspicions down.

[P62]
What had kept her going through the misfortunes that had piled upon her over the past two years was the people around her.

[P63]
They were the greatest inheritance her grandfather had passed to her father, and her father to her.

[P64]
Even as the Yongbong Escort Bureau lost its former glory and gradually declined, they had stayed. Despite her repeated failures, they had continued to show her unstinting trust and support.

[P65]
That was why she hadn’t wanted to suspect them. Why she had refused to doubt them.

[P66]
*But now…*

[P67]
Ju Hwaran swept an empty gaze over her surroundings.

[P68]
Chief Escort Heo Jun stood frozen, looking as betrayed as she felt. Then she saw the other three people who knew about the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng.

[P69]
They were the three outstanding escort captains who represented the Yongbong Escort Bureau—the men collectively known as the Dragon-Phoenix Three Escorts.

[P70]
*Seokchil. Noh Piljung.*

[P71]
Ju Hwaran’s gaze passed over the two middle-aged escort captains, both nearing forty, then turned to the last man.

[P72]
*Song Ilseom.*

[P73]
Unlike the other two members of the Dragon-Phoenix Three Escorts, Song Ilseom was tall and strikingly handsome.

[P74]
Barely past thirty, he had joined the Yongbong Escort Bureau as an escort ten years earlier and risen rapidly through the ranks.

[P75]
Though he occasionally revealed his rough temper, his outstanding martial arts had led numerous escort journeys to success. That was why, despite his youth, he had earned a place among the Dragon-Phoenix Three Escorts.

[P76]
But Song Ilseom was also the subject of endless gossip.

[P77]
> “They say he used to be a wandering martial artist. A fixer, no less.”

[P78]
> “Apparently, there was nothing he wouldn’t do as long as he got paid.”

[P79]
> “That’s not all. Everyone says he’s deeply in love with the Young Lady. Mihyang told me that whenever he gets the chance, he slips into the inner courtyard and wanders around the garden.”

[P80]
> “I heard he joined the Escort Bureau because of the Young Lady… Everyone knows the Chief wanted an escort as his son-in-law, after all.”

[P81]
Ju Hwaran knew the rumors surrounding Song Ilseom.

[P82]
She also knew that most of them were true.

[P83]
Song Ilseom’s blatant stares had made her uncomfortable more than once. Indeed, that was why she had agonized over whether to bring him on this escort journey.

[P84]
*But surely Captain Song wouldn’t…*

[P85]
The moment Ju Hwaran’s gaze settled on Song Ilseom’s face, his thick, fierce-looking eyebrows shot upward.

[P86]
*Flash—whoosh!*

[P87]
“Hwaran!”

[P88]
Three things happened at once.

[P89]
A dagger shot from Song Ilseom’s sleeve.

[P90]
Chief Escort Heo Jun urgently threw himself in front of Ju Hwaran.

[P91]
And finally—

[P92]
*Thud!*

[P93]
“Ghk… Grrrk.”

[P94]
More than twenty jang away, a Black Stone Stronghold bandit collapsed with the dagger buried in his throat.

[P95]
Bloody foam spilled from the bandit’s mouth. He convulsed, then went still.

[P96]
“…”

[P97]
A frigid silence descended over the scene. It seemed as though it might last forever, until Song Ilseom shattered it with a single shout.

[P98]
“No more talking! Fight as if your lives depend on it!”

[P99]
His fierce cry carried far on the night wind.

[P100]
Ju Hwaran, Heo Jun, and everyone else from the Yongbong Escort Bureau realized the same thing.

[P101]
Negotiations were over.

[P102]
Now they would have to fight to the death against hundreds of enemies who had suffered an unexpected opening attack.

[P103]
“Song Ilseom! What have you done?”

[P104]
At Chief Escort Heo Jun’s furious shout, Song Ilseom drew his willow-leaf saber and rested it across his shoulder.

[P105]
“What do you think? It’s a little late to ask that now, isn’t it?”

[P106]
“You bastard…”

[P107]
“He’s right.”

[P108]
Ju Hwaran spoke calmly as she gripped her sword hilt.

[P109]
Unfortunately, Song Ilseom was telling the truth.

[P110]
Heavenly Axe was already advancing toward them, radiating a terrifying aura.

[P111]
One of his men had been killed before he could react, and flames seemed to pour from his bulging eyes.

[P112]
“I’ll slaughter every last one of you.”

[P113]
*Hissssss!*

[P114]
Red qi writhed along the blade of his lowered axe.

[P115]
The Green Forest Alliance had countless members, but Heavenly Axe ranked twentieth among them—a Peak master.

[P116]
Buoyed by their leader’s aura, the five hundred Green Forest bandits growled like wild beasts.

[P117]
“Kill them all!”

[P118]
“This will be your grave!”

[P119]
Listening to their furious cries, Ju Hwaran looked up at the star-studded night sky.

[P120]
*This may be my last escort journey.*

[P121]
Of the seventy-odd people who remained, barely forty were escorts once the caravan porters were excluded.

[P122]
All of them were utterly exhausted from the long journey. The odds were far too cruel for them to face Heavenly Axe and five hundred Green Forest bandits.

[P123]
*Can I do this?*

[P124]
*Thud, thud, thud.*

[P125]
The ground trembled beneath hundreds of footsteps. The battle she had tried to avoid but could no longer escape was about to begin.

[P126]
*All we can do now is fight to the very end.*

[P127]
She had to get at least one person out alive.

[P128]
Just as Ju Hwaran was about to lower her gaze, she noticed a star she had never seen before.

[P129]
Among the countless stars embroidered across the pitch-black sky, one shone brighter than all the rest. It cast its radiance for the briefest moment, then vanished.

[P130]
And in the next instant, something no one could have expected happened.

[P131]
“Everyone, don’t fight! No matter how badly you get along, nothing good will come of fighting!”

[P132]
At the sudden shout, everyone stopped dead. Hundreds of heads whipped toward the source of the voice.

[P133]
The world lay submerged in darkness.

[P134]
Four figures stood atop a hill, faintly illuminated by the moonlight.

[P135]
Then quiet voices drifted down.

[P136]
“What are they?”

[P137]
“They look like bandits. The people on the other side seem to be from an Escort Bureau.”

[P138]
“No, I can see they’re bandits. I’m asking why they’re fighting out here in the middle of the night. We’re already busy enough to drop dead.”

[P139]
“They look busier than we are.”

[P140]
“Mujin, has it been long since you were hit?”

[P141]
“No. About half an hour.”

[P142]
*Smack!*

[P143]
“Gibang, do you know who they are?”

[P144]
“Of course.”

[P145]
“Help me out, Speed Beggar.”

[P146]
“Judging by the flag, they’re from the Yongbong Escort Bureau. The other side is Black Stone Stronghold, led by Heavenly Axe.”

[P147]
“Never heard of either one. But for some reason, Heavenly Axe sounds familiar.”

[P148]
“The Yongbong Escort Bureau was once counted among the Ten Great Escort Bureaus of the martial world. Heavenly Axe is a Peak master ranked twentieth in the Green Forest Alliance. They say he wields a single axe like a demon…”

[P149]
“No, wait. You don’t mean that Heavenly Axe, do you?”

[P150]
“You know Heavenly Axe?”

[P151]
“I definitely killed him… Did he catch the reincarnation bus or something? Wait here. I’m going to get a look at his face.”

[P152]
“Benefactor! What’s a reincarnation bus?”

[P153]
“Try crossing a crosswalk the next time you’re bored.”

[P154]
The utterly incomprehensible conversation ended there.

[P155]
Then a large shadow came trudging down the hill.

[P156]
Only when it drew closer, one step at a time, could everyone make out what it was.

[P157]
*What the hell is that?*

[P158]
*He’s just a young punk. Why is he carrying a pack frame on his back?*

[P159]
It was a truly bizarre sight.

[P160]
Hundreds of people stood facing one another in the darkness, weapons drawn.

[P161]
And through their midst came a young man carrying a pack frame, strolling beneath the moonlight as if he were out for a walk.

[P162]
*Step, step. Stop.*

[P163]
“Sorry to interrupt when you’re so busy.”

[P164]
The young man finally stopped and slowly turned his head.

[P165]
He frowned at the grimy bandits. When his gaze reached Ju Hwaran, he suddenly began fidgeting awkwardly. Finally, he gave Heavenly Axe a quick once-over and tossed out a single remark.

[P166]
“This isn’t the bastard.”

[P167]
“…”

[P168]
“…”

[P169]
Hundreds of pairs of eyes widened at the bombshell.

[P170]
He had just called Heavenly Axe—a Peak master counted among the Green Forest Alliance’s foremost experts—a bastard.

[P171]
While everyone was still doubting their ears, the second bomb dropped.

[P172]
“Oh, you’re that guy. The real Heavenly Axe. No wonder something seemed off. But you don’t look as impressive as the rumors made you sound either.”

[P173]
Heavenly Axe finally came to his senses, his eyes blazing like fire.

[P174]
“Y-You lunatic!”

[P175]
The next instant, the axe in his hand crashed down toward the crown of the young man’s head.

[P176]
*Whoosh—crash!*

[P177]
Condensed qi collided.

[P178]
A flexible sword intercepted the axe blade, which shimmered with red qi.

[P179]
Ju Hwaran’s wrist trembled as she desperately blocked the blow.

[P180]
She, too, was a swordswoman who had reached the Peak. But Heavenly Axe possessed both tremendous natural strength and far greater experience. She was nowhere near strong enough to withstand him.

[P181]
“Ghk! Young Hero, hurry and run—!”

[P182]
“You little bitch, how dare you!”

[P183]
*Clang, clang, clang!*

[P184]
The two weapons ground against each other, scattering sparks.

[P185]
The enormous axe slowly bore down on her.

[P186]
Just as Heo Jun and Song Ilseom rushed forward to help, the young man who had been standing there as if frozen finally spoke.

[P187]
“Say one thing for me.”

[P188]
“…What?”

[P189]
“Help me. Just say those words.”

[P190]
*Is he out of his mind?*

[P191]
The thought flashed through Ju Hwaran’s head.

[P192]
The young man hadn’t even reacted to Heavenly Axe’s attack. If she hadn’t blocked it with her flexible sword, he would have been split in two without a chance to move.

[P193]
But regardless of what she thought, the words were already leaving her mouth.

[P194]
“Help me!”

[P195]
Then she saw it.

[P196]
The faint smile forming at the corner of the young man’s lips.

[P197]
A voice so quiet that only she could hear it reached her ears.

[P198]
“Quest accepted.”

[P199]
*Whoosh!*

[P200]
A scorching wind erupted without warning.

[P201]
And Ju Hwaran felt an endless warmth.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 310

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃310화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|스스스슥.
  6|
  7|천력부의 등 뒤로 모습을 드러낸 산적들의 숫자는 오백을 헤아렸다.
  8|
  9|그러나 주화란의 얼굴이 차갑게 굳은 것은, 그들의 수가 압도적이기 때문만은 아니었다.
 10|
 11|‘기세가 달라.’
 12|
 13|산을 넘으려는 자와 막는 자. 표국과 녹림은 떼 놓을 수 없는 관계다.
 14|
 15|매번 칼을 빼 들 수는 없는 노릇이라 표국 측에서는 일정 금액의 통행료를 지불하고, 녹림 또한 적당한 선에서 물러나 서로의 체면을 지키는 것이 오랜 관례였다.
 16|
 17|그러나 천력부와 그가 이끄는 흑석채의 산적들에게서는 물러서려는 기미가 보이지 않았다.
 18|
 19|“당신은…… 끝내 피를 볼 생각이군요.”
 20|
 21|주화란의 말에 천력부가 입꼬리를 말아 올렸다.
 22|
 23|“어린 년이 눈치가 제법이로구나. 맞다. 내 오늘 흑석산을 피로 물들일 생각이니라.”
 24|
 25|“어린 년?”
 26|
 27|“왜, 마음에 안 들면 늙은 년이라 불러 주랴?”
 28|
 29|“나는 용봉표국의 소국주. 내가 당신에게 하듯, 당신도 예의를 갖추세요.”
 30|
 31|붓으로 그린 듯한 주화란의 아름다운 눈썹이 위로 솟구쳤다.
 32|
 33|용봉표국의 무남독녀지만 금이야 옥이야 자란 것만은 아니다.
 34|
 35|어린 시절부터 손바닥에 굳은살이 배기도록 검을 휘둘렀고, 표사들과 함께 길에서 먹고 자며 보고 배웠다.
 36|
 37|사람들은 강북삼화라며 주화란을 떠받들지만, 그녀는 온실 속 화초가 아니었다.
 38|
 39|“맹랑한 년이로고. 싫다면 어찌하겠느냐?”
 40|
 41|“그렇다면…….”
 42|
 43|비수를 숨긴 꽃, 은비화(隱匕花) 주화란이 서늘한 표정으로 말을 이었다.
 44|
 45|“죽어야지, 어린 년한테.”
 46|
 47|“뭐라? 으허, 으하하하하!”
 48|
 49|천력부의 광소가 멎은 것은 잠시 후였다.
 50|
 51|“생각보다는 강단이 있군. 마음에 들었다.”
 52|
 53|“늙은 산적 놈 마음에 들어 봤자 기쁘지도 않아.”
 54|
 55|“혓바닥이 제법 맵구나. 뒷일이 걱정되지 않느냐?”
 56|
 57|“도대체 왜 이런 짓거리를 벌이는 거지?”
 58|
 59|“왜냐니. 산적이 죽이고 빼앗겠다는데 별다른 이유라도 필요한 것이냐?”
 60|
 61|천력부의 능청스러운 대답에 주화란은 입술을 질끈 깨물었다.
 62|
 63|“이 일이 알려지면 녹림맹의 입장도 곤란해질 텐데.”
 64|
 65|“곤란해져?”
 66|
 67|“우리 용봉표국 또한 정파의 일원. 정파 무림이 가만히 있지 않을 테니까.”
 68|
 69|“정파의 일원이라. 그럼 곤란하지.”
 70|
 71|천력부가 덥수룩한 턱수염을 쓰다듬으며 말을 이었다.
 72|
 73|“그래서 알려지지 않도록 애써 볼 생각이다. 모든 비밀은 새어 나가지 않으면 그만 아니겠느냐?”
 74|
 75|“……!”
 76|
 77|살인멸구(殺人滅口).
 78|
 79|천력부의 말이 뜻하는 바를 알아차린 주화란은 검파를 힘껏 움켜쥐었다. 그런 그녀를 대신해 총표두 허준이 앞으로 나서며 외쳤다.
 80|
 81|“백 냥! 길을 터 준다면 은자 백 냥을 주지. 오늘 일은 불문(不問)에 부칠 테니 이쯤에서 멈추게!”
 82|
 83|“허어. 백 냥이나? 그것도 은자로?”
 84|
 85|“물론. 내가 지금껏 허언을 한 적이 있던가?”
 86|
 87|“그건 아니지. 우리가 한두 번 본 사이도 아니고. 허 표두라면 충분히 믿을 만해.”
 88|
 89|총 표두 허준은 삼십 년에 가까운 세월을 용봉표국에 몸담았다.
 90|
 91|용봉표국은 섬서에 기반을 둔 대형 표국. 그곳에서 크고 작은 수백 회의 표행을 성공시킨 그는 흑석산을 자주 넘나들며 녹림의 채주들과 안면을 텄고, 오 년 전 새롭게 채주가 된 천력부와도 마찬가지였다.
 92|
 93|“평소 통행료의 다섯 배야. 짓궂은 장난은 그만하고 이만 길을 터 주게.”
 94|
 95|“짓궂은 장난이라. 그렇게 보였나?”
 96|
 97|너털웃음을 터트린 천력부의 얼굴에 돌연 한기가 서렸다.
 98|
 99|“사람을 병신으로 봐도 유분수지. 이봐, 허 표두. 값은 제대로 쳐야지.”
100|
101|“가, 값을 제대로 치다니?”
102|
103|“지금 운송 중인 표물에 천년설삼(千年雪蔘)이 있다는 건 우리 산채에서 기르는 개새끼도 알아. 당장 장물로 팔아 치워도 은자 수천 냥은 너끈히 받아 낼 물건이지. 안 그런가?”
104|
105|“……!”
106|
107|그 순간, 주화란과 허준을 포함한 몇몇의 눈꺼풀이 파르르 떨렸다.
108|
109|천년설삼은 완전히 소화한다면 능히 일 갑자의 공력을 얻을 수 있다는 영약.
110|
111|종남파에서 비밀리에 의뢰한 천년설삼의 존재는 용봉표국 내에서도 극소수만이 아는 특급 기밀 사항이다.
112|
113|그런데 어찌 천력부에 귀에 들어갔단 말인가.
114|
115|‘우연이 아니었어.’
116|
117|주화란의 뇌리에 지난 넉 달간의 표행이 스쳤다.
118|
119|철천지원수라도 만난 듯 덤벼들던 산적들과 이름 모를 낭인들.
120|
121|크고 작은 수십 회의 전투를 치르며 큰 희생을 감내해야 했던 이유는 바로 천년설삼에 대한 정보가 흘러 나갔기 때문이었다.
122|
123|‘도대체 누가?’
124|
125|설마 하는 생각은 했었다. 그러나 애써 의심을 억눌렀다.
126|
127|지난 이 년간 겹치고 겹친 악재에서 그녀를 견딜 수 있게 해 준 원동력은 바로 주위의 사람들이었으니까.
128|
129|할아버지가 아버지에게, 아버지가 자신에게 물려준 가장 큰 재산.
130|
131|용봉표국이 과거의 위상을 잃고 점점 기울어지는데도 그들은 떠나지 않았다. 계속해서 실패를 겪는 자신에게 아낌없는 신뢰와 지지를 보여 주었다.
132|
133|그래서 더더욱 그런 이들을 의심하고 싶지 않았다. 의심하기 싫었다.
134|
135|‘하지만 이제는…….’
136|
137|주화란은 공허한 눈빛으로 주위를 훑었다.
138|
139|그녀만큼이나 큰 배신감을 느낀 채 굳어 버린 총표두 허준. 그리고 천년설삼의 존재를 아는 세 사람이 눈에 들어왔다.
140|
141|용봉표국을 대표하는 뛰어난 세 명의 표두. 이른바 용봉삼표(龍鳳三鏢)라 불리는 이들이었다.
142|
143|‘석칠. 노필중.’
144|
145|마흔 줄에 접어든 두 명의 중년 표두를 스친 주화란의 시선이 마지막 한 사람을 향했다.
146|
147|‘송일섬.’
148|
149|송일섬은 용봉삼표의 다른 두 사람과는 달리 훤칠하고 잘생긴 외모의 소유자였다.
150|
151|이제 갓 이립을 넘긴 젊은 나이의 그는 십 년 전 용봉표국에 표사로 입문하여 승승장구했다.
152|
153|간혹 거친 성미를 드러내기도 했으나 뛰어난 무공으로 표행을 성공적으로 이끌었기에 젊은 나이임에도 용봉삼표로 불릴 수 있었다.
154|
155|그러나 그런 송일섬에게는 무성한 뒷말이 따라다녔다.
156|
157|
158|
159|‘낭인 출신이래. 그것도 해결사.’
160|
161|‘보수만 받으면 무슨 짓이든 마다하지 않았다더군.’
162|
163|‘그뿐인가? 아가씨를 깊이 연모하고 있다는 소문이 파다해. 지난번 시비인 미향이가 알려 줬는데, 틈만 나면 내원으로 들어와 정원을 서성거린다더라고.’
164|
165|‘표국에 들어온 이유도 아가씨 때문이라던데…… 다들 아는 사실이지만 국주님께서 표사 사윗감을 원하지 않았나.’
166|
167|
168|
169|주화란도 알고 있었다. 송일섬을 둘러싼 공공연한 소문을. 그리고 그들의 말이 대부분 사실임을.
170|
171|가끔 느껴지는 송일섬의 노골적인 시선에 마음이 불편했던 적도 있었다. 그런 이유로 이번 표행에 그를 기용할지 고민한 것도 사실이었다.
172|
173|‘하지만 설마 송 표두가…….’
174|
175|주화란의 시선이 송일섬의 얼굴에 머무른 바로 그 순간, 사나워 보이는 그의 굵은 눈썹이 위로 솟구쳤다.
176|
177|번쩍, 쐐애애애액!
178|
179|“화란아!”
180|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
